title: Pass loaded config into the scheduled alert pass and prove the disabled path writes nothing

supersedes.reason: T1 approval refused for a fail-open defect: main() loaded the environment then called runScheduledAlertPass without it, so the pass read process.env and a file-configured ALERT_AGENT_ENABLED=false was ignored while detection still wrote to the database. Three evidence contradictions were also correct: two unresolved actionable review threads, a proof claiming a pending review after it had completed, and Linear state disagreeing with the manifest.

sha_binding.verified_source_note: Commit carrying the three ported surfaces plus the fix. Later commits in this lane are proof artifacts only.

scope.port_fidelity: Workflow byte-identical to the superseded head. Implementation differs by the call site plus comment corrections. Tests are a pure append.

static_proof.type_check_scope_caveat: scripts/ is outside every tsconfig project reference, so pnpm type-check does not enforce types in this file. The regression guards are the focused suite and the wiring guard, not the compiler.

runtime_proof.defect_fixed: main() called runScheduledAlertPass(repositories) without the loaded environment, so loadAlertAgentConfig read process.env and file-configured values were ignored. The disabled branch already refused before touching a repository; the flag was simply read from the wrong source.

queries.name: disabled path performs zero writes
queries.method: counting-repository harness wrapping saveDetection, updateNotified, startRun and completeRun, with a counting fetch
queries.result: detections 0, notified 0, runsStarted 0, runsCompleted 0, fetch calls 0; listRecent empty; no alert.detection or alert.notification run recorded
queries.significance: Disabled means nothing happened, not merely that the function returned early.

queries.name: config precedence, measured end to end
queries.method: loadEnvironment() against a file fixture, then loadAlertAgentConfig on the merged object
queries.result: workflow path (process.env=true) -> enabled=true; operator path (variable absent from process) -> enabled=false
queries.significance: Records the exact boundary of this fix rather than the broader claim. See known_limitations.

row_counts.probe: delivery attempts on the disabled path
mutations killed (throw removed / throw moved after detection / call site reverted)

runtime_proof.mutation_testing: Three mutations, all killed. Removing the enabled check fails the two zero-write tests. Moving the throw AFTER the detection pass -- so it still rejects with the same message but writes first -- fails on the WRITE COUNTER, not the rejection, which is what shows the zero-write claim is not self-confirming. Reverting the call site to its shipped form fails the wiring guard.

known_limitations.item: The fix closes the operator path, not the scheduled-workflow path.
known_limitations.detail: ALERT_AGENT_ENABLED is a declared AppEnv key and readEnvValue reads process.env first. The scheduled workflow sets it to 'true' explicitly, so a file-configured false does not disable that job. Measured: workflow path enabled=true, operator path (variable absent from the process) enabled=false. Changing the workflow path means removing that variable from the workflow env, a production-posture change outside this correction.

listRecent orders by current_snapshot_at and applies its limit before the notified=false and window filters. Raising the limit to 2000 narrows exposure but does not remove it; the repair belongs in the packages/db query, outside this lane. Production holds 176 undelivered rows against that limit.

known_limitations.item: The member-channel policy is enforced in this entry point only.
known_limitations.detail: apps/alert-agent calls the notification pass with no injected fetch and would deliver to the member channel unguarded. Dormant — last alerting run 2026-04-28 — and outside this lane.

known_limitations.item: A disabled agent alerts every scheduled run.
known_limitations.detail: The disabled path throws, the entrypoint posts an ops finding and exits non-zero, so disabling reds the workflow. Pre-existing and arguably correct: silent disablement is how the previous outage stayed invisible.

safety_posture.member_delivery: ALERT_MEMBER_CHANNELS_ENABLED pinned to 'false'; both guards read process.env deliberately, because that is what Discord delivery resolves against, so they are unaffected by this change and still fail closed.
safety_posture.sgo_and_ingestion: disabled; zero SGO or ingestion triggers in the workflow
safety_posture.production: parked; no mutation, unpark or secret access in this lane

independent_review.bound_to: Full review at 5610e5af; re-bound by bounded delta verification at 9fb6b98c; this head adds only comment and test-name corrections raised by that re-bind.
independent_review.findings_actioned: The review found the first fix introduced a second config defect -- substituting the allow-list AppEnv for process.env dropped 20 of 22 tuning keys, so ALERT_MIN_TIER=notable would silently become watch. Corrected by merging rather than substituting. The re-bind then found a false comment and an overclaiming test name, both corrected here.
